indicator: Weekly inpatient SARI admissions split by diagnosis group (COVID, INFLUENZA, RSV, PNEUMOKOKKEN, SONSTIGE) and ward (STATION I = intensive care, N = normal ward), with population BEV_ZAHL. INFLUENZA = SARI admissions with an influenza diagnosis.

KW 2023' to '40. KW 2026' (178 weeks). Influenza ICU/normal-ward admissions by season: 2023/24 337/6089, 2024/25 355/6877, 2025/26 362/6895. evidence:
WebFetch of github.com/zeitferne/covidat-tools dldata.toml shows both official URLs (with ?q=now). WebFetch of github.com/garzj/sari-weather-vis shows a README describing sari-data.csv as weekly SARI admissions from sari-dashboard.at open data.

publisher: Robert Koch-Institut (official GitHub organisation; also on Zenodo)

source_name: RKI SARI-Hospitalisierungsinzidenz (ICOSARI): influenza-SARI subgroup, plus all-cause SARI by age in the same file
publisher: Robert Koch-Institut (FG 36), data from HELIOS hospitals data centre
indicator: Weekly incidence per 100,000 of new hospital admissions with SARI (ICD-10 J09-J22 as principal diagnosis) that also carry ICD-10 J10 (influenza, virus identified) as principal or secondary diagnosis ('Influenza'). Extrapolated to Germany from about 70 sentinel hospitals, which cover 5-6% of national admissions. The same file has all-cause SARI ('Gesamt') by age from 2014-W40, but that series is not influenza-specific.
age_breakdown: Influenza subgroup: all ages (00+) only. All-cause SARI (Gesamt): 00+, 0-4, 5-14, 15-34, 35-59, 60-79, 80+. COVID-19: 00+, 60-79, 80+ (from 2020-W10). RSV: 00+ only.
format: GitHub (TSV); also Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.23232217 and OpenCoDE
caveats:
These are the same data ERVISS publishes for Germany. ERVISS DE sari_plus equals the Influenza subgroup, and ERVISS DE sari_rate equals Gesamt 00+.
ERVISS DE sari_flu_positivity is sari_plus/sari_rate, i.e. the share of SARI cases coded J10, not a lab positivity.
ERVISS DE sari_flu_tests is a pseudo-count: it equals sari_rate multiplied by a near-constant (median 42.1, max 42.4, over 224 weeks), so it is not a real number of tests or cases.
The Influenza subgroup is ICD-coded, so it depends on coding practice and is not lab-confirmed in the surveillance sense. Recent weeks are revised.
The Influenza subgroup first appeared in the repo on 2024-10-10 (commit 04d9ec9), not 'around November 2024'. Before that commit the file had a single SARI_Hospitalisierungsinzidenz column (total SARI by age).
The Influenza subgroup is published neither by age nor for seasons before 2020/21. All-cause SARI for 2014/15-2019/20 by age is not in ERVISS, but turning it into a flu series needs an external influenza share, which would make it a modelled series.
evidence:
Read the local clone (working copy, not kept, commit aeea125 of 2026-10-08) and the full history (rki_sari_hist, 207 commits from 2023-09-28). WebFetch of the GitHub page confirmed J10 in principal or secondary diagnosis, CC BY 4.0 and 207 commits.
Row counts per subgroup and age: Influenza|00+ 314 rows (2020-W40 to 2026-W40); RSV|00+ 314; Gesamt 627 rows in each of 7 age groups (2014-W40 to 2026-W40); COVID-19 344 rows each for 00+, 60-79 and 80+.
Recomputed against the ERVISS clean file:
- Influenza vs ERVISS sari_plus: 209 weeks, max absolute difference 0.154, mean 0.027.
- Gesamt 00+ vs ERVISS sari_rate: 314 weeks, max 0.3, mean 0.064.
- 2025-W05: Influenza 15.2 vs sari_plus 15.16; Gesamt 32.3 vs sari_rate 32.4.
- ERVISS detections/tests reproduce sari_flu_positivity to within 0.05 percentage points.

source_name: WHO FluID VIW_FID_EPI mirror, Apr-2025 download (GitHub cobeylab/transformer-flu-forecasting, data-raw/VIW_FID_EPI.csv)
publisher: Third-party copy of the WHO FluMart export (Cobey lab, U Chicago). Original publisher: WHO.
indicator: All-cause SARI_CASE (2024+ WHO column naming), SARI_INPATIENTS, SARI_POP_COV and SARI_DEATHS by age group. There is no ORIGIN_SOURCE or ISO2 column.
surveillance_type: Sentinel hospitals; AT national (about 9.1M population covered)
format: GitHub CSV (67 MB, 529 830 lines; 22 lines are malformed and need on_bad_lines handling)
caveats:
The most recent FluID copy found. It adds 2023/24 and part of 2024/25 for EU SARI countries, and adds AT (from 2023-W19), CY (2023/24+), EE (2022/23+), GR (2022/23+, total only), LV (2024/25) and FR (2020/21-2021/22, max 43 per week). All are all-cause SARI and duplicate ERVISS SARI submissions; only FR is absent from ERVISS SARI.

TOTAL ROWS ARE INFLATED:
- 'ALL' rows, and also many 'All' rows, equal the sum of every age row including overlapping bands.
- Examples: DE 2021-W02 ALL = 1492 vs 753 from non-overlapping bands (763 in the 2023 copy). IE 2023-W01 All = 64 vs 15TO64 + 65TO = 32 (the 2023 copy has 32). AT 2024-W01 ALL = 5187 vs 2819. BE 2012-02-20 All = 68 vs 55 in the 2023 copy.
- The median ratio of total to non-overlapping sum is 1.5-2.0 for AT, BE, DE, EE, ES, HR, IE, MT, RO and SK, and 1.0 for GR (which has no age bands).
- So recompute totals as 0TO4 + 5TO14 + (15TO64 or 15TO29+30TO64) + (65TO or 65TO79+80TO) + UNKNOWN. A fresh download from the WHO endpoint probably has the same issue.
evidence:
Cloned read-only to [local working copy] (HEAD 2026-04-15) and extracted the CSV to .../hosp_sources/verify_fluid_cobey/.
- Ran verify_fluid_new.py and verify_fluid_alltotal.py. EU max week start is 2025-04-21.
- The repo's R/process_WHO_data/script1_process_VIW_FNT_FID.R reads this file and filters AGEGROUP_CODE 'ALL' or 'All', so that downstream code inherits the inflation.
- With totals rebuilt from non-overlapping bands, new/old ratios against the 2023 copy are 1.00 (median) for DE, ES, HR, MT and LT.
